result.description:
Position: Construction Project Manager
Position Type: Full Time
Salary: $110,000 - $130,000 p.a plus Super
Employer Name: J & DE HOMES PTY LTD - T/a JDE HOMES
A.B.N. 24 614 743 789
Job Location: Level 2, 207 Pulteney Street, Adelaide, SA, 5000,  AUSTRALIA
Advertising Period: 28 days - 13 Jul 2026 > 10 Aug 2026

Please include Reference: J1697-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Summary

Our client JDE Homes is seeking to add a Construction Project Manager to its South Australian construction and development team. The company delivers fixed-price property construction, development and project management services across residential, civil, industrial and commercial projects. This role will support the planning, coordination and delivery of technically challenging building projects, while maintaining quality, budget, safety and completion requirements.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:

- Plan, organise and manage construction projects from commencement through to practical completion.
- Coordinate project resources, including labour, subcontractors, materials, plant and equipment.
- Interpret architectural drawings, construction plans, engineering details and technical specifications.
- Monitor project budgets, timelines, quality standards, risks and contractual obligations.
- Liaise with architects, engineers, consultants, clients, subcontractors and relevant authorities.
- Manage procurement scheduling and ensure materials are available to meet construction milestones.
- Supervise site progress and ensure works align with approved plans and specifications.
- Coordinate inspections, approvals and documentation required by councils and regulatory bodies.
- Ensure adherence to workplace health, safety, building and performance standards.
- Negotiate with suppliers, subcontractors and stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.
- Prepare project reports, progress updates, cost reviews and construction documentation.
- Manage project variations, delays, defects and implementation of corrective actions.
- Lead subcontractors and site teams to achieve quality and programme outcomes.
- Support tender preparation, contract administration and construction methodology recommendations.
- Maintain professional communication with clients to support cost-effective project delivery.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:

- Minimum ten years of relevant experience in construction project management or building project delivery.
- Strong ability to manage residential, commercial, civil or industrial construction projects from start to finish.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating subcontractors, trades, consultants, suppliers, plant, equipment and site resources.
- Sound knowledge of construction drawings, specifications, building processes, safety obligations and quality standards.
- Proven ability to monitor project costs, budgets, schedules, risks, variations and completion deadlines.
- Strong communication skills for liaising with clients, architects, engineers, authorities and internal project teams.
- Practical experience resolving construction issues and recommending cost-effective building methods or project solutions.
- Ability to work without direct supervision while maintaining accurate project records and professional standards.

Please include Reference: J1697-Workforce in the Subject Line and email all applications and CV to apply@jobsource.net.au

Due to the volume of applicants, only those meeting the minimum standards will be considered and only successful applicants will be contacted.  Thank you for your interest in the role.
result.title: Construction Project Manager

result.description: AGROVISE  Due to continued business growth, we are seeking a motivated and experienced Agricultural and Agritech Technician to join our team. The successful applicant will support the installation, commissioning, operation, testing, maintenance and optimisation of agricultural technology systems and equipment, while assisting with irrigation management, precision agriculture, crop production technologies, field trials, technical data collection and the delivery of innovative agritech solutions across a range of agricultural projects in Western Australia.   Benefits   Competitive salary package of $80,000 – $100,000 plus superannuation.   Ongoing training and professional development in agricultural technology, irrigation and automation systems.   Opportunity to work with innovative agricultural, water and renewable energy projects across Western Australia.    Task & responsibilities   Examine topographical, physical and soil characteristics of farmland to assist in determining optimal land use and identifying nutrient deficiencies.   Assist Agricultural Research Scientists and Agronomists in developing improved methods of planting, fertilising, irrigation, harvesting and crop management to maximise productivity.   Identify plant diseases, pests, fungi and weeds affecting agricultural production and assist in implementing appropriate control measures.   Provide technical advice, training and support to clients on agricultural technology solutions, including sensors, remote monitoring systems, farm management software and automation technologies.   Install, configure, program, test, commission, repair and maintain advanced agricultural technology and equipment, including irrigation controllers, pumping systems, sensors, telemetry, automation and precision agriculture systems.   Develop, operate and maintain integrated agricultural technology systems used in irrigation, water management and farm production, including analysing operational data and preparing technical reports.   Conduct field testing, equipment inspections, fault diagnosis and preventative maintenance to ensure efficient operation of agricultural infrastructure and agritech equipment.   Collect, record and analyse technical and operational data to evaluate system performance and recommend improvements.   Prepare technical documentation, maintenance records, installation reports and service schedules.   Work collaboratively with engineers, project managers and clients to deliver innovative agricultural infrastructure and technology solutions while ensuring compliance with workplace health and safety requirements.    Qualification & experience   Certificate IV, Diploma or higher qualification in Agricultural Technology, Agricultural Engineering,  or a closely related discipline.   At least one year of relevant industry experience (more experienced applicants are encouraged to apply).   Experience working with irrigation systems, pumps, agricultural equipment or automated control systems.    About Company    Agrovise is a Western Australian engineering and agritech company specialising in greenhouse infrastructure, protected cropping and agricultural technology solutions. The company designs, installs and maintains greenhouse systems, irrigation and fertigation infrastructure, climate control and automation systems, helping commercial growers improve productivity, water efficiency and sustainable farming practices across Western Australia. result.description:
Lead electrical mining projects from concept to commissioning while enjoying a 5:2 roster   Your new company  
 Our client is a leading Australian resources organisation with a strong commitment to operational excellence, safety, and sustainable project delivery. With a substantial portfolio of capital projects and ongoing investment in site infrastructure, they offer the opportunity to work on complex projects within a collaborative and high-performing team environment. 
   Your new role  
 As an Electrical Project Manager, you will be responsible for managing electrical capital projects through the full project life cycle, from early studies and detailed design through to construction, commissioning, and handover. You will work closely with consultants, contractors, and key stakeholders to deliver projects safely, on schedule, and within budget. 
 Key responsibilities include: 
 
 Managing electrical projects from concept development through to completion 
 Coordinating consultants during feasibility studies, engineering, and detailed design phases 
 Managing project budgets, schedules, risks, and reporting requirements 
 Overseeing contractors and ensuring compliance with contractual obligations 
 Leading project execution, construction activities, and commissioning works 
 Reviewing and managing project documentation, technical deliverables, and governance requirements 
 Collaborating with operations, maintenance, engineering, and external stakeholders 
 Ensuring all work is delivered in line with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements 
 Driving project performance and continuous improvement outcomes 
 
   What you'll need to succeed     
 
 Demonstrated experience managing electrical projects within mining, resources, heavy industry, energy, or infrastructure environments 
 Proven experience managing consultants through study, design, and project delivery phases 
 Strong understanding of project delivery methodologies and project governance requirements 
 Experience managing contractors during construction and commissioning activities 
 Sound knowledge of contract administration and contractor management 
 Strong stakeholder engagement, communication, and leadership skills 
 Ability to manage multiple project priorities in a dynamic operational environment 
 Electrical trade or engineering qualifications will be highly regarded. 
 Commitment to maintaining the highest safety standards 
 
   What you'll get in return  
 This is an excellent opportunity to join a highly regarded mining operation and contribute to the successful delivery of critical electrical infrastructure projects. You'll work on a Monday-to-Thursday site roster with the flexibility to work from home on Fridays, while camp accommodation is provided throughout your assignment. Both FIFO and DIDO options are available, offering flexibility for candidates across Queensland. You'll join a supportive team environment where your expertise will directly influence the success of key site projects and future growth initiatives. 
   What you need to do now  
 If you're interested in this role, applications can be submitted via the "apply now" button. Please ensure you are submitting an up-to-date CV. If you have any further questions, please call Jennah Murray 07 4960 1129. 
   
 If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.  Please  click here  to apply.
